source: Bush, R. 2010. 'Large Ruminant Nutrition Theory, Part 1: Revision and Physiology', University of Sydney (mekonglivestock.wordpress.com). NOTE: source PDF has a font/ligature encoding quirk (e.g. 'ti' rendered as '/', double letters rendered as 'A' or similar) -- text below has been decoded from this consistent, mechanical substitution pattern, not guessed.
text: For fattening cattle and buffalo, the guidance gives concrete quantities: animals need at least 15% of their body weight in fresh, good-quality feed every day, so a 200kg bull needs at least 30kg of fresh feed daily -- with an extra allowance since as much as 25% of forage offered can be lost to spillage, meaning roughly 800-1,000 square metres of grass growing area is needed to fatten one adult bull. Water needs are tied to body size: cattle and buffalo drink at least 10% of body weight per day, so a 200kg bull needs about 20 litres daily (more than two full buckets), with higher needs in hot weather or when eating more dry feed. Fresh, clean water must be available in the pen at all times. The six basic steps to fattening given are: plant and maintain forage; provide feed and water troughs; deworm and vaccinate; provide feed and water ad libitum (as much as the animal will eat); apply 'smart feeding' (improving feed quality, not just quantity); and other supporting practices such as fattening pens and coordinated marketing.
